response.original_title: Quaintance: A Thousand Years of Dreams
response.overview: A documentary exploring the life, art, and elusive legacy of George Quaintance (1902–1957).  During the repressive 1940s and 1950s, Quaintance became a trailblazer of queer visual culture. Working from his Arizona studio, Rancho Siesta, he painted idealized, muscular men—often cowboys and classical heroes—that defined the aesthetics of early physique magazines and influenced generations of artists.  Following his sudden death in 1957, most of his paintings and sculptures vanished into obscurity. The film follows a dedicated group of collectors, archivists, and art restorers—including Charles Leslie, Ken Furtado, and Kamila Korbela—on a detective-like quest across the United States to track down, authenticate, and preserve his missing masterpieces, restoring the story of a visionary artist who lived boldly ahead of his time.
